title: 7-round AES-192: split-variable collision attack, complete key

target.description: AES-192 on 128-bit blocks, reduced to 7 rounds. The collision is between internal byte-valued functions under the same unknown round keys, not between two AES master keys. Recover the initial four guessed bytes and twenty late-round bytes; peel the recovered final round, apply the six-round method and continue until the entire master key is recovered, with additional work described as negligible. The standard target is AES-192; the source repeatedly prints 196 despite listing 192 among the permitted key lengths in its introduction.

setting.key_relation: One unknown standard AES master key; no related-key or known-key access.
setting.key_population: general secret key; no restriction to a weak-key family
setting.plaintext_model: All 2^32 values of four plaintext bytes, with twelve others fixed. For each initial-key guess use about 2^16 induced c values and sixteen y values per c.
assumptions: The source describes right-going ShiftRow. Standard AES uses left-going shifts. Reindexing columns by J(r,c)=(r,-c mod 4) conjugates the independent-round-key construction; inputs, outputs and recovered round keys are reflected consistently before standard key expansion. This coordinate normalization is a local structural interpretation, not a complete attack reproduction.
The four c-dependent internal constants are modeled heuristically as a random 32-bit function of the chosen three-byte c value; collision probabilities use this model.

time.note: Section 4.1's heading reports approximately 2^140 complexity without explicitly naming its operation unit there. No exact conversion from the pair loops, table sorting or partial computations to full AES encryptions is asserted.

data.note: The same acquired structure is reused for the collision search and subsequent round peeling.

memory.reported: Two families of 2^80 sixteen-byte lists per c, and a sorted pair table; peak not priced
memory.note: Keep the source's precomputation shapes. A 2^80-entry temporary table alone is not the whole peak when all c-dependent tables are retained.

preprocessing.reported: Ciphertext-dependent tables for each c and both ten-byte key halves
preprocessing.note: The source describes these precomputations inside the search but does not separately price a complete setup budget.

success.description: Section 4.1 states about one-half probability that the selected c-set yields a useful internal-function collision and hence the correct key material; full-key recovery then follows by round peeling. This is a heuristic estimate, not a physical or software trial frequency.

evidence.interpretation: Primary-source endpoint preserving the stated target, access model, native resource units and recovery scope. Paper-local pagination is distinct from the whole-proceedings PDF page number.
